reason: The RTL behaviour the finding describes is real: a resetUsefulCnt pulse that arrives while needReset=1 is absorbed (needReset is already set, the sweep Counter has no restart path and there is no pending-request bit, IttageTable.scala:181-189), so sets 0..k-1 already passed by the in-flight sweep are not written again, and tickCnt is zeroed by that pulse regardless (Ittage.scala:395-398). However, this does not violate R-ITTAGE-5 as worded ('the reset request must never be deferred indefinitely or lost'): the second request is coalesced into a sweep that is in progress and that does run to completion (needReset only clears on resetFinish, i.e. after the last set is written), so it is neither lost nor deferred by the second pulse; the divergence is from the refuter's stricter expectation (a full re-sweep of sets 0..k-1), not from the requirement text. Its only effect is that useful bits legitimately re-set in the already-swept sets during the window survive until the next tick reset, a bounded heuristic-quality effect, and the structure (free-running reset index, set-and-clear doing_reset flag) is the classic TAGE coalescing idiom, so it is arguably intentional. Reachability of the specific input is also doubtful: it needs every cycle between the sweep reaching set 127 and pulse P to have req.fire=1 or table-0 update.valid=1 while >=255 mispredicted indirect trains are processed, and each of those mispredictions is a backend redirect; if a redirect bubbles the BPU s1 stage for even one cycle without a coincident table-0 update (Bpu.scala, outside this block), the 128-set sweep finishes and the second pulse starts a fresh full sweep, satisfying the required result. If the requirement owner reads 'lost' as 'every distinct pulse must produce a complete clear of all useful bits', the mechanism part of this finding stands and the verdict should be re-judged as CONFIRMED on the mechanism with the reachability caveat above; the sweep being starvable by continuous req.fire is a separate issue not created by the second pulse.
reachability: State class (needReset=1, resetSet=k>0, second pulse) is real under the default config (TickWidth=8, Parameters.scala:36; NumBanks=2, Parameters.scala:30; table 0 nRows=256, Parameters.scala:24) and no parameter folds it away; the pulse producer (Ittage.scala:378-379, 395-398, 402) is independent of sweep progress and req.valid is s1_fire && true.B (Ittage.scala:190-191) with req.ready=1 after power-on (IttageTable.scala:239), so the block cannot exclude a stall at k=127. The exact cycle pattern of the failing input (zero table-0 idle cycles from resetSet=127 until P across >=255 mispredict-redirects) depends on BPU redirect behaviour outside src/main/scala/xiangshan/frontend/bpu/ittage/ and looks infeasible if each redirect yields one s1 bubble; not verifiable within the allowed scope.
